h: The Real Houdini and North Manchester Days Out
p: The name is a clever nod to Harry Houdini, the world's most famous escape artist. Born Erik Weisz in Budapest in 1874, he grew up in the United States and became a superstar in the early 20th century, wriggling out of handcuffs, straitjackets and locked trunks, sometimes while hanging upside down or submerged in water. He even challenged police forces to lock him up, and he usually escaped. It's a fun story to share with the kids before you go, and might inspire them to channel their inner Houdini when the clock is ticking.

With the rooms suitable for younger children, this is a great choice for a family birthday. To make the most of it, chat to the team when booking about which room might suit your group's age and experience. If you've got very young children, consider making teams of mixed ages, so older siblings or grown-ups can help when a puzzle gets tricky.

Make sure everyone knows the basic rules before you start. Don't force anything, as puzzles never need brute strength, and keep an eye on the timer so you know when to ask for a hint. After the game, take a few minutes to talk about how you solved things and what you'd do differently next time. Kids love reliving their big moments.

When you're done, Heaton Park is a short drive north, a huge green space with a boating lake, woodland, play areas and the grand Heaton Hall at its heart. It's perfect for a picnic or a run-around after an hour of puzzling. Football fans can head east to the Etihad Stadium, home of Manchester City, for a stadium tour, and Manchester city centre is close by for museums, shops and food.
